finding: The printed first diagram asserts a short exact sequence of Hausdorff locally convex spaces, with left map the global two-zero-mode theta realization multiplied by the positive half-norm; the second is the norm-one isotype sequence, described as nuclear Fréchet and later as linearly and topologically exact. These assertions are announced here. The later Global Converse Theorem argues fixed-character closed range in the unshifted Mellin coordinate, which must be shifted by +1/2 for the twisted arrow. It does not by itself supply simultaneous global preimages. This is a partial landing on the actual left arrow: for all represented rational adelic LF tests with both polar modes zero and class theta invariant under the rational norm-one subgroup, the exact half-twisted theta profile is a linear element of the genuine all-real-weight radial Schwartz stage. Iterating the real dilation generator with the weight shift and using the existing two-mode tails controls every weighted Schwartz seminorm on each bounded LF family. The map kills precisely the original class-theta kernel, so it realizes the algebraic injection of the radial theta quotient, without proving continuity on its intrinsic quotient, a closed range/topological embedding, full LF exactness, or nuclearity. This is not an L² completion or a fixed unramified source. See .godel/formalize/rational-theta-weighted-stage.md for source cross-checks and the remaining lifting problem.
retry: For the rational trivial isotype, formalize continuity on the intrinsic two-mode quotient and use the accepted finite-unit average to reduce to finite-unit invariant tests. Show that these have even real unramified representatives with the same global theta and both zero modes zero; then prove a Schwartz-seminorm estimate for a representative from the ambient weighted theta seminorms (the two-tail Poisson estimate in the handoff is one candidate). For full LF closed range, give a simultaneous lift of a stage-supported limit with compatible angular components into one permitted source stage, with estimates adequate for that stage's Schwartz topology, or a different direct range characterization. Separately identify the quotient-isotype topology by compatible continuous projectors and establish nuclear Fréchet properties, not just closedness in a Hilbert space.
